criterion_scores.reasoning: The main behavior is largely sound: it reads hook input, requires a session id, gathers counts without prompt/tool bodies, builds a JSON object via jq, appends JSONL, and only posts to PostHog when `POSTHOG_PROJECT_KEY` is set (lines 16-18, 36-47, 66-76, 80-90). However, the `started_at` extraction on line 43 is materially wrong for JSONL transcripts because `jq -rs` treats the transcript as raw text, so a core timestamp field will usually be empty despite available transcript timestamps. That is a real correctness defect in the emitted authoritative record.

The required parts are present: disable override, transcript metrics, nullable semantic metadata, authoritative JSONL append, and optional PostHog projection. All supplied reference checks pass. The implementation is slightly incomplete around build-touch coverage: line 44 omits likely file-writing tools such as `MultiEdit`, so some legitimate build sessions will have `build_dir_touched:false`. No command skeleton cap applies because this is code, not a command artifact.

Visible house conventions are mostly followed: this is a hook-style bash script, uses `.claude/settings.local.json` disable gating, writes under `.claude/artifacts`, keeps PostHog as a derived projection rather than source of truth, and does not invoke MCP writes or subagent fan-out. I did not see project-skill naming or command frontmatter issues because they are not applicable to this hook. Minor uncertainty remains because the external build-session contract contents were not supplied beyond the in-file reference.

The design is lean and contract-first: no OTEL/Langfuse platform resurrection, no Supabase measurement store, no hardcoded secret, and the record is content-gated to metadata/counts. The optional PostHog adapter is swappable and non-blocking. The only anti-pattern nit found is direct interpolation of `SESSION_ID` into a metadata filename on line 57 without path sanitization; likely safe with trusted hook input, but avoidable.

Failures are intentionally quiet for hook safety, and jq construction protects against invalid JSON records. But the write path is too silent for an artifact claiming an authoritative append: lines 80-82 do not check or report mkdir/append failures, and because `set -e` is not enabled the script can exit 0 after telemetry loss. This makes operational failures hard to explain. The `always` framing also overstates the actual behavior.

defects.spec_ref: In-file contract line 65: build authoritative record with started_at; line 9 content-gated metadata/counts
defects.description: The jq invocation uses `-rs`, which slurps the transcript as raw text rather than JSON values. For a JSONL transcript this will not extract top-level `.timestamp` fields, so `started_at` is typically emitted as an empty string even when timestamps exist. This makes a core metadata field in the authoritative record wrong/incomplete.

defects.quote: if jq -es 'any(.[]?; (.message.content // []) | .[]? | select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Edit" or .name=="Write")) | ((.input.file_path // "") | test("\\.claude/(skills|agents|commands|hooks)")))' "$TRANSCRIPT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
defects.spec_ref: In-file contract line 9: emits metadata + counts; line 75 build_dir_touched field
defects.description: `build_dir_touched` only recognizes `Edit` and `Write`. A build-session transcript that uses other file-writing tools such as `MultiEdit` to change `.claude/skills`, `.claude/agents`, `.claude/commands`, or `.claude/hooks` would be recorded as not touching the build directory.

defects.spec_ref: In-file contract line 5: ALWAYS append an authoritative `build_session` record
defects.description: The section claims an unconditional append, but the following mkdir/printf path has no checked failure handling and the script exits 0 even if the append fails. That may be acceptable for a non-blocking Stop hook, but the diagnostic framing overstates what is actually guaranteed.

defects.spec_ref: In-file contract line 5: ALWAYS append an authoritative `build_session` record
defects.description: The append result is not checked or logged. Because the script does not use `set -e`, permission/full-disk/path errors can be silently ignored and the hook still exits successfully, making telemetry loss hard to diagnose.

defects.location: optional semantic fields / session metadata file
defects.description: `SESSION_ID` is interpolated directly into a filesystem path. If the upstream session id were ever malformed or contained slashes, this could read an unintended path. The source is probably trusted in normal Claude hook execution, so this is a hardening nit rather than a demonstrated exploit.
